title: The Surface of the Earth and Fossils
seo_title: Primary 6 Basic Science and Technology: The Surface of the Earth and Fossils Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 6 Basic Science and Technology: Learning About Our Environment
standard_text: The Earth's surface is made of rock and soil. Weathering breaks rock into small pieces, which are carried away and deposited in layers that harden into sedimentary rock. Fossils are the remains or traces of plants and animals that lived long ago, preserved in rock; Africa has many important fossil sites. (summary of the Basic Science and Technology curriculum, Primary 6, theme: Learning About Our Environment)
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 Basic Science and Technology worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Learning About Our Environment): rocks and soil, weathering and erosion, sedimentary rock, how fossils form and rock layers and fossils. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Sedimentary rock forms from layers of sediment.
key_sub: Fossils are found mostly in sedimentary rock.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Earth has a thin outer layer called the crust, made of rock. Wind, water and temperature changes break rocks into small pieces (weathering). Soil is a mixture of tiny rock pieces, humus (rotting plants and animals), air and water.

Rivers carry sand and mud and drop them in layers. Over millions of years the layers are pressed and cemented into sedimentary rock, such as sandstone and shale. When a dead plant or animal is buried in sediment, it can become a fossil. Rocks in many places, including parts of Nigeria, hold fossils of ancient sea animals, and caves in Africa have fossils of early humans.

Example

In undisturbed rock layers, which layer is the oldest?

Layers pile up over time.

Answer: the bottom layer

Example

Which kind of rock usually contains fossils?

It forms in layers.

Answer: sedimentary rock

Common mistakes

  • Thinking fossils form quickly.
  • Thinking soil is just broken rock.
  • Thinking fossils are found in lava rock.

items.q: How does a fossil form? This happens: “The soft parts rot away, leaving bones or shell.” What happened just before?
c: More layers build up and press the sediment into rock.
Its body is quickly covered by mud or sand.
Minerals slowly replace the bones, turning them to stone.
Millions of years later, the rock wears away and the fossil is found.
items.e: Order: dies → covered → soft parts rot → layers press → minerals replace → found.
